en: Pulling down on a fixed pulley's rope lifts a heavy bucket upward by changing the direction of the applied force.
The deep grooves on car tire treads increase friction with the wet road, preventing the vehicle from sliding.
The Moon's gravitational pull on Earth's oceans causes the water to bulge, creating high and low tides.
Running an electric current through a wire coiled around an iron nail temporarily magnetizes the nail to pick up paperclips.
Closing a switch completes an electrical circuit, allowing electrons to flow through the wire and light up the bulb.
A glass prism bends incoming white light at different angles, separating it into a rainbow of distinct colors.
Striking a drum's tight skin creates rapid vibrations that push air molecules, sending sound waves to your ears.
Leaving a metal spoon in hot soup transfers thermal energy from the liquid to the handle through direct conduction.
Releasing a stretched rubber band converts its stored potential energy into kinetic energy, snapping it forward rapidly.
Pushing a steel axe downward forces its sharp wedge shape apart, splitting the wood fibers with multiplied force.
Sitting near a campfire warms your skin because the burning wood emits infrared radiation that travels through the air.
A red apple absorbs all light colors except red, which it reflects into your eyes to appear red.
